chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: The Jones Beach ten-piece band and his Dunbar Palace men
summary: He led a ten-man band at a Jones Beach club after an audition, and at the Dunbar had trumpeter Jack Butler and drummer Manzie Johnson. Tape 1 ends.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, there's a night club there. I've got to think of the name of this club. This is where I had a big band and we would commute. (unintelligible)

I had ten men. Excellent band. I think this happend, if I'm not mistaken, before I went into the Dunbar Palace. Right, because we did an audition for -- you had to make a few auditions, you know, to get the job. And of course, the night club operator didn't think anything about having another band over in the corner fighting after

you played your time. And they would judge, and you had to actually sell yourself for the job, you know, and -- but I had some good guys. They were New York musicians and were more or less experienced. It didn't take us long. They were good readers, these guys, and in fact, I've got a picture of a group that I had (inaudible) at Dunbar. They were guys that (inaudible) you evidently have heard some of these fellas. There's a guy that was a trumpet player [Jacques] in my band named Jack Butler. He went to Europe, and everything else. He's still in New York. A great trumpet player, and he was a member of my band. There was a drummer named Manzie Johnson -- you ever heard of that name?

He played with a lot of the greats there. He was on a lot of record sessions with Coleman Hawkins -- he was my drummer. I don't know if I'm gettin' ahead of myself or not, but -- this is how (inaudible) my getting into the band field on my own.
I tell you what, I'm gonna have to change tapes here, so why don't we take a break, you haven't even had any of your (unintelligible) here.
Well, there's something going in. (inaudible) End of tape 1
